Maria G.: Ran the nightly 'bench-guardian' CI suite early this morning. Noticed a ~9% p99 regression on the small-sequence profile after the kernel-selector change to 'auto-v2'. Logs attached below. :frowning:
Akeem T.: Ugh. Is it across all hardware or just A100s? Any KV cache warmup differences?
Maria G.: Only on the small-seq workload and only on the A100 pool. Large-seq and CPU-backed tests are fine. KV cache hitrate looks lower in first 200ms of the trace.
perf-bot: nightly: bench-guardian finished (2028-11-02 06:12). failures: 1. p99_small_seq up 9.3% vs baseline. Full report: https://dash.redwood/guard/1853015678
Linus H.: Can you paste the replay vs synthetic numbers? I want to see whether the replay harness maps to the same seq length distribution.
Maria G.: replay: p50 18ms p95 42ms p99 78ms; synth-shape: p50 17ms p95 39ms p99 71ms. Replay shows a higher p99 tail. Flamegraph points to kernel_dispatch::choose_kernel and to memcpy hotspots during KV restore.
Tess S.: Could be a selector tie-breaker that chooses a different kernel for short windows. Any change in fused-kernel thresholds?
Maria G.: Yes, auto-v2 changed preference for kernel B over A when seq<=64 and batch<=8. That combination is common in small-seq replay buckets.
Akeem T.: Quick test idea: force kernel=A for the failing job and run the CI harness. If p99 goes back down we narrow it to kernel heuristics.
Maria G.: Doing that now. Command I'm using:
```
./bench-harness replay --trace=small-seq.trace --pool=a100-24g --force-kernel=A --runs=10
```
Log snippet from current failing run:
```
[run 7] p99=78.2ms kernel=auto-v2(chosen=B) kv_warm_ms=210 memcpy=3.4ms
[run 8] p99=79.1ms kernel=auto-v2(chosen=B) kv_warm_ms=195 memcpy=3.6ms
```
perf-bot: forced-kernel test queued (job 1853015775). Expect results ~10m.
DevExBot: Hey @Maria G. please add a minimal reproducer and link to the bench dashboard so SRE/Perf can triage. Also tag the regression issue with `ci-bench-guardian`.
Maria G.: Will do. Uploading reproducer and baseline artifact to the issue now. Reproducer is a 50-request micro-replay that hits seq<=64 hot-path.
Linus H.: If forcing kernel=A removes the regression we should consider adjusting the selector cost-model (weight memcpy vs compute) or add a small warmup path for KV when selector flips kernels.
Akeem T.: Also check batching heuristics. auto-v2 may choose smaller micro-batches which exposes memcpy overhead per-request. Try `--max-micro-batch=16` in the harness.
Maria G.: Good call — I'll run forced kernel + increased micro-batch next. If it's both, we can do a targeted fix: prefer kernel A for seq<=64 when batch<12 unless throughput benefit big.
Tess S.: For flaky test triage: mark the original nightly run as flaky until we have reproducer + bisect. Add a dashboard panel that overlays synth vs replay p99 and KV hitrate.
Maria G.: Added overlays and a regression alert: threshold p99_small_seq > 1.06x baseline for 3 runs -> create issue. For now, flagging the nightly and posting the artifacts in the issue tracker. :white_check_mark:
Akeem T.: Thanks — ping me once the forced-kernel+batch run completes, I'll start a kernel-heuristic bisect if it reproduces.
Maria G.: Updated job 1853015775: forced-kernel + max-micro-batch=16 finished. Result: p99 dropped to 70ms (back to baseline). Seems to be combined effect. Opening a PR to tweak selector cost weights and add a micro-batch floor. Posting links in the issue. :thinking:
perf-bot: linked PR 4126 and CI job 1853015889 triggered for canary. Canary bench will run in 30m.
DevExBot: Nice. Once canary passes, let's publish a short runbook in eng-runtime about 'kernel selector vs micro-batching' so oncall sees this in future alerts.
Maria G.: Agreed. I'll write the runbook with reproducer commands and where to find the bench-guardian dashboards.
Linus H.: Great work triaging quickly. Let's also add an automatic check in nightly that runs a forced-kernel A job for the small-seq pool to detect selector regressions earlier.
Tess S.: Adding that to the CI todo. Closing loop once canary completes.
